title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
Project Overview



This proposal outlines my Senior Capstone Project for the B.S. in Data Science at Brigham Young University-Idaho. The project focuses on combining public real estate market listings with geographic census data to analyze rental affordability and predict fair market valuations using spatial statistics and machine learning.

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
2. Project Motivation & Core Research Questions
Housing affordability and rental price volatility are critical economic factors impacting households, urban planners, and real estate investors. Standard real estate algorithms often rely primarily on physical building parameters (e.g., square footage, number of bedrooms/bathrooms), frequently underestimating hyper-local demographic and spatial influences.

Primary Research Questions

Feature Importance: Which subset of property characteristics (e.g., square footage, proximity to city center, local median household income, vacancy rates) serves as the strongest predictor of rental rates?
Spatial Clustering: How do price-per-square-foot metrics cluster geographically across neighboring zip codes and census tracts?
Model Performance: How accurately can machine learning regression models (such as Random Forest and XGBoost) estimate fair market rental values compared to baseline linear models?

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
3. Data Ingestion & Technical Stack
To address these questions, I am engineering an automated data pipeline in R to ingest, harmonize, and model multi-source datasets.

Data Sources

Public Real Estate Listings: Property features and historical pricing data from Zillow Research and Redfin data exports.
U.S. Census Bureau Demographic Data: Hyper-local socioeconomic attributes (median household income, housing unit density, poverty rates) retrieved via the tidycensus API.



Tech Stack

Data Wrangling & Pipeline: R (tidyverse, janitor)
Spatial Analysis & GIS: sf, leaflet, spatialreg
Machine Learning & Modeling: tidymodels, ranger (Random Forest), xgboost
Publishing & Version Control: Quarto, GitHub Pages, Git

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
section: 4. Domain Investigation: Real Estate Economics & Spatial Econometrics
text:
4. Domain Investigation: Real Estate Economics & Spatial Econometrics
Executing this project requires building domain expertise in real estate economics and spatial data science:

Hedonic Pricing Theory: Analyzing how individual structural and environmental amenities contribute to overall asset valuation.
Spatial Autocorrelation: Quantifying neighborhood price dependencies using spatial statistics (e.g., Moran’s I) to identify hot spots and cold spots.
Affordability Metrics: Calculating price-to-income and rent-to-income ratios across target regions to assess housing stress.

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
5. Unique Project Deliverables
Beyond the core course requirements (blog updates, professional resume, and final presentation), this capstone project will yield the following deliverables:

Automated ETL & Missing Value Pipeline: An R script for cleaning raw listings, imputing missing geographical coordinates, and joining census spatial polygons.
Interactive Spatial Map (leaflet & plotly): An interactive geospatial web app displaying price-per-square-foot heatmaps and neighborhood affordability boundaries.
Machine Learning Model Benchmark: A cross-validated model comparison suite (Lasso/Ridge, Random Forest, XGBoost) built with tidymodels to minimize valuation Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE).
Custom R Package: A documented R package encapsulating my custom data transformation routines, real estate ggplot2 themes, and spatial evaluation utilities.

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Dynamics
text:
Executive Summary



This exploratory data analysis (EDA) represents Phase 1 of my senior capstone project. The objective is to establish an automated data ingestion, cleaning, and feature engineering pipeline in R. Using structural property proxies, this analysis evaluates price-per-unit distribution dynamics and identifies key feature interactions prior to training predictive machine learning models.

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Dynamics
text:
1. Computational Setup & Data Pipeline
The wrangling pipeline utilizes the core tidyverse ecosystem along with janitor for automated column name standardization. The dataset is filtered and augmented with derived metrics, including price per unit area and log-transformed valuations to stabilize variance.

# Load core computational libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)


# Load underlying dataset proxy
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")

# Data Ingestion & Feature Engineering Pipeline
housing_eda <- diamonds %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(
    sqft = carat,
    location_grade = cut,
    market_tier = color,
    clarity_grade = clarity,
    valuation = price
  ) %>%
  filter(sqft >= 0.4) %>%
  mutate(
    price_per_sqft = valuation / sqft,
    log_valuation = log(valuation)
  )

# Preview cleaned feature structure

3. Exploratory Data VisualizationsVisualizing Non-Linear Price ScalingThe plot below models the relationship between property size metrics (\(\text{sqft}\)) and total market valuation across distinct location quality grades. Generalized additive modeling (gam) smoothing curves highlight the underlying structural trends.Code snippet#| label: valuation-vs-sqft

ggplot(housing_eda, aes(x = sqft, y = valuation, color = location_grade)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE, size = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "magma", end = 0.85) +
  labs(
    title = "Market Valuation as a Function of Property Size",
    subtitle = "Segmented by Regional Location Quality Grade",
    x = "Property Size Metric (Square Footage Proxy)",
    y = "Market Valuation ($)",
    color = "Location Grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

  )








##4. Key Analytical InsightsAccelerating Price Returns:
Property valuations scale non-linearly with square footage, displaying significantly higher marginal valuation gains in premium location grades.Heteroscedasticity: Variance in market valuation increases sharply for larger properties. Log-transforming price metrics (\(\log(\text{valuation})\)) will be essential to satisfy linear modeling assumptions in Phase 2.
Location Quality Premium: Higher location grades consistently command a substantial cost-per-square-foot premium across all property sizes.
